first_impression.reaction: Went to the FAQ first, as usual. Short, practical answers, no sales pitch in them, so I went back up. The intro is a bit soft, but the takeaways are actual checks (finish the plan first, confirm power and weather rules), which is what I want from a how-to. Kept reading, skimmed the decor ideas, read the practical and destination sections properly.

journey.quote: It suits couples who want the entrance to the reception to feel considered, and it works for 40 guests as well as 200.
journey.reaction: Says who? Nothing later backs those two numbers up. Not a deal breaker, but it reads like a line someone made up to sound specific.

journey.quote: Finish the table plan first, because every interactive display is only as reliable as the list behind it.
journey.reaction: Sensible and unglamorous. Good sign that it isn't just a mood board.

journey.section: Finish the Table Plan Before You Choose a Display
journey.quote: Build it in [Wonderland Studio](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-studio), our planning app for seating charts and RSVPs, so the list you send to the stationer or the screen is the same list your RSVPs produced.
journey.reaction: At least it says 'our' app, so I know it's a plug. Is it free? What's the catch? Nothing here tells me.

journey.quote: Few things welcome a guest more warmly than a glass with their name on it.
journey.reaction: Feelings, not information. The next paragraph about bar staff and non-alcoholic options is the useful bit.

journey.quote: This one needs staff to pour in time and keep the tray topped up, so arrange it with the venue's bar team.
journey.reaction: Good, it tells me the hidden cost driver: staff time. That's the catch I'd have asked about.

journey.section: A Screen or QR Lookup on Arrival
journey.quote: Never rely on a phone alone.
journey.reaction: Honest about the weak point of the flashiest option. That's the kind of trade-off I trust.

journey.section: A Screen or QR Lookup on Arrival
journey.quote: If you are choosing software to build the plan, our guide to [comparing seating chart apps](https://weddedwonderland.com/expert-advice/prismm-vs-wonderland-studio) sets out the differences.
journey.reaction: The link says Prismm vs Wonderland Studio. So it's a comparison written by the company that owns one of the two apps, and the sentence doesn't say so. I'd assume it's rigged until proven otherwise.

journey.quote: If you would like someone to bring the display, the table plan and the styling together for a celebration overseas, a conversation with our [Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=our-favourite-interactive-seating-charts&utm_content=primary) team is a good place to start.
journey.reaction: Sales pitch dropped in the middle, before the practical section. It's polite and short, so I just scrolled past it.

journey.quote: The [Queensland Government accessible events guide](https://www.qld.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0030/470865/queensland-government-accessible-events-guide.pdf) treats signage as central to helping people move through a venue, and asks that it be clear, logical, accurate and accessible.
journey.reaction: An actual government source I can open and check. Best part of the article for me.

journey.quote: Digital displays change in seconds; handwritten mirrors and printed walls do not.
journey.reaction: Clear trade-off. Useful for deciding, not just for looking at.

journey.section: Interactive Seating Charts at a Destination Wedding
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor confirms inclusions in writing before you commit, so these answers are settled before the design is.
journey.reaction: In writing is the right answer. Doesn't tell me what I'm paying for that, though.

journey.section: Plan It with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Your Advisor works in your time zone and plans venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world.
journey.reaction: 'Payments' is where my radar goes off. If you're handling vendor payments, do you take a cut from the venue? And 'anywhere in the world' is a big claim with nothing behind it on this page.

unanswered_questions: Is Wonderland Studio free, or is there a paid tier or catch?
Who wrote the Prismm vs Wonderland Studio comparison, and is it independent?
Roughly what does each style cost compared with a plain printed board? Nothing on the page gives a sense of cost.
Does Wedded Wonderland take commissions or mark-ups from venues or suppliers when the Advisor handles vendors and payments?
What does the Wedded Concierge fee actually buy for something as small as a seating display?

turn_offs_found.quote: Few things welcome a guest more warmly than a glass with their name on it.
turn_offs_found.why: Emotional line standing in for a fact. Minor.

turn_offs_found.quote: For a smaller wedding, a photograph of each guest with a short handwritten note and their table number is hard to beat for warmth.
turn_offs_found.why: Same again, 'hard to beat' is an opinion dressed up as a verdict. The practical tip after it is fine.

turn_offs_found.quote: If you are choosing software to build the plan, our guide to [comparing seating chart apps](https://weddedwonderland.com/expert-advice/prismm-vs-wonderland-studio) sets out the differences.
turn_offs_found.why: A vendor comparing its own product to a rival without saying so in the sentence. That's the 'hidden catch' marketing I look out for.

would_share_with: My partner, for the practical details and the destination venue question list
Whoever ends up doing the stationery, for the readability and accessibility section

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready to talk it through, start a conversation with [Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=our-favourite-interactive-seating-charts&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: I came for seating chart ideas, not a planner, and the article answered that. The CTA isn't pushy and comes after useful content, but nothing here tells me the fee model or whether you take supplier commissions, so I've got no reason to click today. I'd save the page, not enquire.

top_3_changes: Say plainly that the app comparison involves your own product. Old: "our guide to [comparing seating chart apps](https://weddedwonderland.com/expert-advice/prismm-vs-wonderland-studio) sets out the differences." New: "our guide to [comparing seating chart apps](https://weddedwonderland.com/expert-advice/prismm-vs-wonderland-studio) sets out how Prismm differs from our own Wonderland Studio."

Swap the emotional line for the practical point. Old: "Few things welcome a guest more warmly than a glass with their name on it. Set filled flutes" New: "A glass with each guest's name on it doubles as the welcome drink. Set filled flutes"
Drop the unsupported guest numbers in the intro. Old: "and it works for 40 guests as well as 200." New: "and the ideas below cover both small and large guest lists."

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction quotes an exact sentence from 05-draft.md
Stayed in character as Daniel (sceptic): FAQ first, looked for sources, trade-offs, catches and commissions
No invented brand facts; Wonderland Studio pricing, comparison authorship, fee model and commissions listed as unanswered questions
[[VERIFY]] markers and HTML comments (image slots, fact tags) ignored
Per orchestrator, fees, commissions, supplier sourcing and vetting not raised as must-fix; suggested edits are exact old/new strings with no new facts or measurements

open_questions.question: Daniel's enquiry blocker is commission and fee transparency near the 'vendors and payments' CTA line; this is deferred brand business detail, so is it logged for the CTA landing page rather than this post?

Top change 1 names Prismm in body copy (taken from the existing internal link slug). Confirm naming a third-party app is acceptable under the no-competitor-branding rule; if not, use "sets out how another app differs from our own Wonderland Studio."

assumptions: Daniel arrived via a Google search for 'interactive seating chart wedding' while working out his own reception details, not while actively shopping for a planner.
Persona is provisional (not CRM-calibrated), so reactions reflect the card, not real data.
